subject.title: Feature request: message delete (revoke) action for WhatsApp channel

question: Should WhatsApp expose bot-owned delete/revoke as `delete`, `unsend`, both, or not at all, and what safety/live-proof requirements must gate the feature?
rationale: This is a destructive action over an authenticated WhatsApp session, and code alone cannot decide the product contract, accepted server-behavior risk, or required live proof for expired-window and group-participant edge cases.

options.title: Sponsor the linked implementation path with safety gates
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/70813 or a replacement for agreed action naming, own-message/fromMe enforcement, LID-aware routing, group handling, expired-window errors, and live WhatsApp proof before landing.

options.title: Narrow the feature to local or explicit cleanup only
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a smaller contract that avoids recipient-visible revoke guarantees until WhatsApp server behavior is proven.

options.title: Reject programmatic WhatsApp retraction
options.body: Close the request as unsupported if maintainers decide the false-success and destructive-mutation risk is not acceptable for agents.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the linked implementation path with safety gates
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/70813 or a replacement for agreed action naming, own-message/fromMe enforcement, LID-aware routing, group handling, expired-window errors, and live WhatsApp proof before landing.
